svg.title: A Halloween evening that welcomes everyone

text.tspan: Everyday English - B1 - 2026/10/31 - 01 - Essay
A costume creates a playful Halloween character.
Pexels · 29225548
A Halloween evening that welcomes everyone
There is more than one way to prepare a Halloween evening. In my experience, practical preparation and attention to
others are two useful starting points.
One reason is that planning the route and the costumes helps everyone stay comfortable. For instance, we check
that costumes allow clear vision and choose a well-lit route. This prevents a small difficulty from taking over the
experience. It also leaves us more time to notice what is happening.
Another reason is that clear choices make sharing treats more considerate. For example, we keep ingredient
information available and offer a non-food option. This approach recognises that the experience belongs to more
than one person and that different people may need different things.
These examples show why preparation and consideration work well together. We do not have to control every detail.
We can make a sensible arrangement and remain ready to respond.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a focused main idea. Develop one supporting reason in each body paragraph, with a concrete
example. Conclude by connecting the two reasons without introducing a new argument. Use the structure as a model; write
about an experience of your own.
Apply the idea to a real situation, then answer: What two reasons support the main idea? Explain one example. (Model: The
two reasons are that planning the route and the costumes helps everyone stay comfortable and that clear choices make
sharing treats more considerate. One example is that we check that costumes allow clear vision and choose a well-lit route.)
